title: Marine Combat Instructor (GySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0311, 0313, 0321, 0331, 0341, 0352, 0363, 0369), CG TECOM
raw_text:
3. MOS 0913, Marine Combat Instructor (GySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0311, 0313, 0321,
0331, 0341, 0352, 0363, 0369), CG TECOM

    a. Summary. The Marine Combat Instructor instructs and assists in the
training of basic combat skills to entry level Marines to include weapons
handling, automatic weapons, munitions, combat conditioning, land navigation,
communications, offensive/defensive tactics and scouting/patrolling. The
Marine Combat Instructor reinforces core values instilled in recruit training
by setting the superior example with professional conduct, knowledge,
bearing, attitude, and provides student performance counseling.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1326.6 CH 1.

        (2) Must meet the standards screening checklist of special
assignments per MCO 1326.6 CH 1.

            (3) Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body fat standards.

        (4) Must be able to achieve a second class on the final Marine Corps
physical fitness test given at Marine Combat Instructor School.

        (5) Must be able to achieve a second class on the final Marine Corps
combat fitness test given at Marine Combat Instructor School.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Marine Combat Instructor Course (M03U2A4)
Camp Lejeune, NC or (M10U2A2) Camp Pendleton, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
Individual Training Standards.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

body:
Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to identify Marines who possess skill sets to conduct vital training, particularly to entry-level Marines, as required by various high visibility Marine Corps programs. First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

3. MOS 0913, Marine Combat Instructor (GySgt to Cpl) EMOS (0311, 0313, 0321, 0331, 0341, 0352, 0363, 0369), CG TECOM a. Summary. The Marine Combat Instructor instructs and assists in the training of basic combat skills to entry level Marines to include weapons handling, automatic weapons, munitions, combat conditioning, land navigation, communications, offensive/defensive tactics and scouting/patrolling. The Marine Combat Instructor reinforces core values instilled in recruit training by setting the superior example with professional conduct, knowledge, bearing, attitude, and provides student performance counseling. b. Prerequisites (1) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1326.6 CH 1. (2) Must meet the standards screening checklist of special assignments per MCO 1326.6 CH 1. (3) Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body fat standards. (4) Must be able to achieve a second class on the final Marine Corps physical fitness test given at Marine Combat Instructor School. (5) Must be able to achieve a second class on the final Marine Corps combat fitness test given at Marine Combat Instructor School. c. Requirements. Complete the Marine Combat Instructor Course (M03U2A4) Camp Lejeune, NC or (M10U2A2) Camp Pendleton, CA. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to Individual Training Standards.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
